data.headline: Lead Tools
data.about:
Driven lead programmer with 15+ years experience building game development tools. Passionate about UX and optimising workflows, working closely with users to make sure they have everything they need to build the best games possible. 

4+ years experience leading a multi discipline team, fostering a collaborative and open environment. 

Exceptional communication and problem-solving skills with a hands on, lead by example style.
data.addressWithCountry: Greater Guildford Area, United Kingdom United Kingdom

description.text:
• Led a tools/build team of six, encouraging group brainstorming and sparking discussions amongst the team over feature development, code architecture and UX of the tools.

• Built a supportive team culture through coffee catch ups, team lunches and always making time for my team.

• Provided mentoring and constructive feedback through 1:1’s, instilling a growth mindset in my team members.

• Proactively reached out and worked extremely closely with coders, artists and designers to ensure myself and my team understood their workflows, upcoming requirements and any day-to-day issues they were hitting.

• Effectively juggled the priorities of features, bugs, support requests and optimisations amongst my team using a combination of Kanban, support slack channels and robust Jira feature request and bug reporting workflows.

• Actively involved in improving the studio culture, collaborating on studio values, taking part in mentoring partnerships.

• Provided technical direction for the studio's tools with a particular focus on workflows and iteration times, recent examples include: 
        • Transitioning our tools to support quick iteration in testing multiplayer game sessions.
        • Improving prefab opening times (from minutes to seconds) with a new open prefab in session 
           feature.

• Collaborated with a range of disciplines to design and coordinate the work to deliver larger scale features, examples include:
        • Moving our game data out of perforce, what this meant for our workflows and how it needed to 
           be integrated within our tooling.
        • Switching from traditional perforce depots to stream depots and adopting a feature branch 
           workflow.
        • Brainstorming and coordinating the tooling required for our new animation node graph system.

• Managed my time to ensure I could remain hands on with our codebase, debugging support issues, fixing bugs, finding optimisations and developing new features.

• Worked on our in-house level editor Creator, building the architecture from the ground up using C# / WPF.

• Took ownership of the design and implementation of many core features, including live edit systems on PC / PlayStation DevKits, widgets, cameras, proxies, property editing, treeviews, asset browsers and many custom controls.

• Assisted in the design and brainstorming of our revolutionary lockless editing system Delta, this feature allowed multiple users to edit the same level data at the same time without the fear of losing work.

• Developed and took full ownership of a brand-new workflow tool LsStart. The goal of this tool was to simplify the setup, update and launch of our tools and assets. It utilised an on-demand sync approach which hid the complexities of perforce away from users whilst also avoiding lengthy sync times and wasted hard drive space. This was especially useful for external partners and remote workers, it also made setting up new hires extremely trivial.

• As part of my work on LsStart I also took full ownership of managing our outsource tools workflow, coordinating with our IT department and external partners to setup Perforce Edge servers and ensuring our tools were working correctly for other studios.

• Collaborated with the build engineers to design and architect pre-submit, a system which allows users to remotely test their changes before they are submitted to perforce. I developed the client-side solution of pre-submit including the frontend.

• Periodically optimised memory usage of our level editor, fixing memory leaks and avoiding large Garbage Collection times as the project data grew.

• Constantly worked on improving the responsiveness and performance of our tools using multi-threading and C#’s Task Parallel Library (async, await).

• Worked on an in-house level editor used by external developers to create content for the PlayStation Home platform.

• Added support for live viewing of levels on PS3 devkits.

• Designed and coded a template system for easy creation of common objects in Home, for example furniture, pets etc.

• Developed an Inspect feature which allowed Home users to view and buy the clothing and accessories worn by other players.

• Created example scripts to showcase how developers could create their own multiplayer games, playable in any Home lobby.

• Provided tools support to external developers creating content for the PlayStation Home platform.
Working in the RnD department of Kuju Entertainment. Developing and maintaining engines and tools.
